title: The STE lint masks a double-backtick code span as one span
why: lint/ste_lint.py MASK_PATTERNS' inline-code entry (a run of non-backticks between single backticks) mis-pairs a double-backtick span, so the rest of the paragraph lints unmasked and some long sentences hide from STE001. Seen in docs/decisions/red-run-trailer-on-test-commits.md item 1a on #1745: a 32-word sentence went unreported. CI's ste-lint shares the pattern (lane notes-fix-large-3, 04:41 CST Nov 8).
note: Fix: the inline-code mask pairs a run of N backticks with the next run of exactly N, as CommonMark does. Red case first: a paragraph with a double-backtick span and a sentence over the limit after it is reported. Control: a single-backtick span masks as today. Queue fix (owner 13:20 CST Nov 7). Filed 04:43 CST Nov 8; Lane notes-fix-large-3, which found it, builds it (coordinator, 04:42 CST Nov 8; owner item 386). Fix the mask in lint/ste_lint.py and in CI's ste-lint copy, from one home if the two share the pattern. Ready as draft #1914 (head a78262f08), base main: INLINE_CODE_RE in lint/ste_lint.py masks double-backtick spans, one home for MASK_PATTERNS and _FIX_MASK. Red cases 1f4c23042 and 28e54d56f. Record: round 1 haiku FAIL, round 2 sonnet PASS, fix check haiku PASS; lane lint PASS (lane, 05:23 CST Nov 8). Follow-up: step backtick-mask-one-home.
